values.value: Thinking about the MARKETING EMAILS that would be rebuilt as target-side templates and content assets — how many templates are in real use, how much of each is custom modules and HubL logic rather than standard modules and copy, and how many language variants are maintained?

[{"value":1,"label":"A large template and module library that emails are assembled from, with HubL macros, includes and loops doing real logic inside the email, and every template maintained in several language variants."},{"value":2,"label":"A meaningful set of custom modules and HubL snippets in the emails \u2014 conditionals, includes, personalisation well beyond tokens."},{"value":3,"label":"Mostly drag-and-drop from standard modules; HubL confined to simple personalisation tokens."},{"value":4,"label":"Templates and copy only, few enough to rebuild deliberately, with personalisation that is merge fields and nothing more."}]

Ask for email templates used in the last 12 months, modules ranked by usage IN EMAILS, and how many templates exist in more than one language. Landing pages, site pages, blog and HubDB are not counted here — whether they are even moving is the cms_scope_expectation probe.
Useful to have to hand: how many email templates you have used in the last 12 months, which custom modules appear in those emails, and how many of the templates exist in more than one language.

skills/mce-mcn-helper/references/framework-reference.md — "Content Builder -> Marketing Workspace (Rebuilt). No automated migration. Templates must be rebuilt manually", and "Cloud Pages -> Experience Cloud pages / LWC (Bridge or rebuild). No direct equivalent"; docs/specs/tier-2/sfmc-next-target-adapter.md — personalization.ampscript unsupported, dynamic_content_blocks partial, i.e. the target's personalisation primitives are merge fields, Calculated Insights and Einstein slots. HubL and custom modules are source-side platform knowledge held by the authoring consultant, which is precisely what interview_only posture declares. THE BANDING IS DELIBERATELY ONE HARSHER THAN migration-accelerator/instrument/migration-accelerator/pairs/hubspot_to_sfmc.yaml's slot 4, and stays so after the rescope: migration-accelerator/capabilities/platforms/hubspot.yaml, hubl_templating severity_by_target — "SFMC Next: there is no scripting language at all, so expressive HubL escalates toward blocker" — which is why custom modules plus expressive HubL sit at 2 here and at 3 there. THE RESCOPE, applied here for the same reason it was applied there: HubL and custom modules span two migrations. Marketing emails are rebuilt on the target by this engagement and are correctly scored; landing pages, site pages, blog and HubDB-driven pages are HubSpot CMS, which a marketing-automation migration does not move — so scoring readiness on them marked a client down for content nobody was proposing to touch. HubDB has left these anchors and is asked instead, unscored, as cms_scope_expectation in migration-accelerator/instrument/migration-accelerator/supplements/hubspot_context.yaml, which this pack already fires; the hubdb_dependency callout below is reframed to read as conditional on that answer rather than as an assumed blocker.
